title: Resistance, Progeny, Population, Germplasm, and Release Workbook
purpose: Provide controlled records for resistance screening, progeny testing, population maintenance, germplasm preservation, and pedigree/release claims.

sections.title: Disease and Pest Resistance Screening Record
fields: Pest reproduction or pathogen load if measured
qualityRules: No visible symptoms alone do not prove genetic resistance.
Separate resistance from tolerance and disease escape.
Document pathogen or pest identity and challenge conditions before comparing lines.
sections.decisionPrompt: Does the candidate repeatedly reduce infection, damage, reproduction, or performance loss relative to appropriate checks under confirmed challenge?

sections.title: Progeny Test and Combining Ability Record
sections.decisionPrompt: Does the parent show repeatable value across relevant mates and environments, or is the result specific to one cross?

sections.title: Population Diversity and Bottleneck Control Record
fields: Effective population size estimate if used
qualityRules: Census size and effective population size are not interchangeable.
Unequal family contribution can create a bottleneck even in a large crop.
Preserve contribution records instead of assuming visible diversity equals genetic diversity.
sections.decisionPrompt: Are enough unrelated contributors represented with sufficiently balanced reproductive contribution to preserve the diversity needed by the breeding objective?

sections.title: Seed and Germplasm Preservation Record
sections.decisionPrompt: Is the accession being preserved as both viable material and a genetically representative sample rather than merely kept alive?

sections.title: Pedigree, Generation, Naming, and Release Claim Record
qualityRules: Names do not substitute for identity records.
Generation labels do not prove uniformity, stability, or commercial readiness.
Pedigree percentages should not be inferred from names alone.
Marketing language must not exceed the available breeding, trial, identity, or laboratory evidence.
sections.decisionPrompt: Can every public claim be traced to a specific identity record, generation history, and supporting evidence?

qualityRules: Keep observational, experimental, and release records distinct.
Preserve negative results, failed regenerations, and uncertainty.
Do not promote draft evidence into a release claim without explicit review.
Use permanent IDs so names can change without breaking identity.
Keep publication authorization separate from scientific completeness.
